brand: Cold-Chain Guard | Design Master Solutions, LLC | QEMU + simulated sensor

scenes.title: QNX 8.0 boots in QEMU and checks itself
scenes.say: A fridge alarm must explain what happened, and what it could not observe. This is Cold Chain Guard on QNX eight in QEMU, with the boot shown sped up. The sensor is simulated, and this is a software prototype, not a medical device. During boot, the target runs our checks, and each one reports its result on this console.

scenes.title: The fridge is a file: /dev/fridge0
scenes.say: Now the console is live. We start the guard with a synthetic excursion. A resource manager exposes slash dev slash fridge zero, so an ordinary cat returns temperature, validity, alarm state and escalation level. A monotonic timer delivers pulses to the dispatch loop. This alarm is active, at escalation level three, and the second read confirms it.

scenes.title: Limits change atomically, or not at all
scenes.say: Writing to the same device changes all limits in one step, and the next sample evaluates them, so this alarm clears. Now an invalid command, with the low limit above the high one. The write fails, and the limits stay as they were.

scenes.title: Advice comes early. It cannot silence the alarm
scenes.say: Next, a warming fixture. The forecast fits a linear trend and offers advice before the limit is reached: alarm zero, trend to high, with an estimate. It is advice only. When the temperature crosses the limit, the real alarm fires. A forecast cannot delay, suppress or clear it.

scenes.title: Kill the daemon: SLM restarts it
scenes.say: Now the daemon runs under System Launch and Monitor, at fixed priority twenty. We kill it. S L M reports the abnormal exit and restarts it, and a different process serves the device. Its clock and alarm state start over, and the audit records one explicit unknown gap, instead of inventing what it never saw.

scenes.say: On the host, the portable modules build with strict warnings and sanitizers. These are real lines from this run. They support the target evidence; they do not replace it.

scenes.title: The audit from that boot, verified on the host
lines: Exported over the QNX serial console
Checksum, audit chain, byte equality with a host replay of the same CSV
scenes.mono_cmd: python3 tools/host/fgctl-extract.py build/console.log build/audit.bin build/fgctl build/ref.bin
scenes.say: The audit from that same boot left the target over the serial console. The checksum verifies the transfer, the verifier checks the chain, and a host replay of the same scenario must match every byte, which also catches a truncated replay. It proves integrity only: a live log still needs an external trusted anchor.

scenes.title: Reproduce it. Then take it to hardware.
lines: Next: physical probe, persistent media, external notifications
Prototype only • no vaccine-safety or clinical claim
scenes.say: Hardware sensing, power loss validation, external notifications and a staff acknowledgement interface remain future work. Our public source and companion codelab show how to build and boot this with your own licensed SDP. Built by Design Master Solutions, LLC.
